&2010
Metropolia leads with a 10 percent volume share of total theses.
Health and welfare fields dominate, representing nearly one third of all output.
Engineering remains the second most significant field of academic production.
Academic output is highly fragmented among the top ten participating institutions.
Social and business studies round out the top three research focus areas.

&2011
Oulun ammattikorkeakoulu takes the top position in annual thesis production.
Health and social fields maintain a strong lead in thematic volume.
Engineering and business remain consistently high-volume research sectors.
Output shares across the top ten universities are relatively balanced.
Cultural studies show a minor decrease compared to the previous year.

&2012
Metropolia returns to the leading position for total thesis production.
Health and social fields continue to capture over one third of share.
The top four institutions produce nearly one third of all institutional output.
Business and administration shows steady growth in research volume.
Engineering studies account for roughly 24 percent of the total output.

&2013
Metropolia extends its leadership with a 10.7 percent share of total output.
Health and social sciences remain the dominant research field by volume.
The research landscape is characterized by stable institutional concentration at the top.
Business and social science fields hold one fifth of the total share.
The gap between the top institution and others continues to widen slightly.

&2014
Metropolia maintains dominance while other institutions exhibit minor fluctuations in rank.
Health and welfare sectors comprise one third of total research production.
Business and social science fields show a slight, steady increase in share.
The distribution of research output remains heavily skewed toward a few sectors.
Engineering output sees a marginal relative decline in percentage share.

&2015
Metropolia increases its influence, securing 11.1 percent of all theses.
Health and social fields reach 34.4 percent of the total output share.
Engineering and business fields together account for over 40 percent of production.
Top-tier universities demonstrate clear, sustained growth in thesis output.
Institutional output distribution is concentrated among ten primary providers.

&2016
Metropolia consolidates power, reaching 11.7 percent of the total volume.
Health and social field nomenclature shifts, reflecting evolving reporting standards.
Business, administration, and law emerge as a primary, high-growth research cluster.
Institutional concentration increases, distancing the top universities from the remainder.
Technical fields show a noticeable adjustment in relative thematic share.

&2017
Metropolia further grows its share, capturing 12.4 percent of total output.
Health and welfare fields hit a new high at 37.2 percent share.
Institutional concentration remains high, with the top four holding significant influence.
Engineering share continues a slight downward trend in overall percentage.
Small field categories remain marginal, comprising less than one percent each.

&2018
Metropolia remains the primary institution with 11.9 percent of total theses.
Health and welfare continue to lead, representing over 36 percent of output.
Business and engineering sectors maintain stable, high-volume contributions to the total.
Tampere and Turku emerge as key competitive players in total volume.
IT and computing fields begin to show clear, upward growth signals.

&2019
Metropolia output remains steady, holding over 11 percent of total research share.
Health and welfare fields slightly decrease in share but remain dominant.
IT and computing studies show continued growth, reaching 7.7 percent share.
Institutional rankings at the top exhibit minimal volatility year over year.
Business and engineering sectors demonstrate consistent, stable research activity levels.

&2020
Metropolia leads despite a marginal decline in total institutional share.
Business and administration fields show a significant jump in overall production.
Health and welfare reach a plateau, representing 34.4 percent of output.
Institutional distribution remains highly stable among the top ten providers.
IT and computing maintain their upward trajectory in thematic significance.

&2021
Metropolia maintains the lead while Haaga-Helia rises in institutional ranking.
Health and welfare dominate, reclaiming over 35 percent of total share.
Business and administration continues to capture nearly 23 percent of output.
The top ten universities account for a consistent majority of total production.
IT and computing fields remain a stable, high-growth sector of research.

&2022
Metropolia output share adjusts downward to 10.9 percent of total volume.
Health and welfare sectors remain the primary focus of student research.
Business and administration continues its high-volume output at 23.3 percent.
Top-tier universities are increasingly bunched together in percentage share.
Engineering and IT fields maintain consistent, long-term stability in total volume.

&2023
Metropolia retains top status while Laurea shows significant growth in share.
Health and welfare output hits a new high in absolute volume.
IT and computing reaches 8 percent share, signaling sustained digital focus.
Institutional competition intensifies among the second through fifth-ranked universities.
Engineering continues as the third largest pillar of research output.

&2024
Metropolia stays dominant but with a lower relative share of total output.
Health and welfare fields consolidate, capturing 35.7 percent of all theses.
IT and computing growth accelerates to 8.6 percent, reflecting industry trends.
Institutional distribution is more balanced, with several universities nearing 7 percent.
Engineering fields see a notable rebound in absolute thesis numbers.

&2025
Metropolia accounts for 10.4 percent of a larger total thesis pool.
Health and welfare fields maintain absolute dominance at 36 percent share.
IT and computing reach an all-time high of 9.4 percent share.
Institutional output gap narrows, suggesting more distributed research volume trends.
Business and health sectors combined represent over half of all research.
